A particle travels in a straight line. Its velocity $\dot{x}$ at time $t$ is given by

$$\dot{x}=\left(3t^2-12t+9\right)\ \text{metres per second}$$
Find the expression for the particle's displacement $x$ in terms of $t$, if the particle was initially at $x=2$.
items.sol:
$$\begin{aligned} x&=\int\dot{x}\,dt \\ &=\int\left(3t^2-12t+9\right)dt \\ &=t^3-6t^2+9t+C \end{aligned}$$
Initially ($t=0$) $x=2$:
$$\begin{aligned} 2&=0^3-6(0)^2+9(0)+C \\ C&=2 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore x=t^3-6t^2+9t+2 \text{ metres}$$

items.part:
A continuous random variable $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$f(x)=\begin{cases}3^{-x}\ln 3 & \text{for } x\ge 0\\ 0 & \text{for all other values of } x\end{cases}$$
Find the exact value of the third quartile.
items.sol:
The third quartile $Q_3$ satisfies $F(Q_3)=0.75$:
$$\begin{aligned}1-3^{-x}&=\dfrac{3}{4}\\ 3^{-x}&=\dfrac{1}{4}\\ -x\ln3&=\ln\dfrac{1}{4}=-\ln4\\ x&=\dfrac{\ln4}{\ln3}\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ Q_3=\dfrac{\ln4}{\ln3}$$

items.part:
A substance decomposes at a rate that is proportional to the mass of the substance remaining. The remaining mass (M) can be modelled using the formula $M=M_0e^{-kt}$, where $t$ is the time in hours, $M_0$ is the initial mass and $k$ is a constant.

Initially there is 30 kg of the substance. After 24 hours half of the substance has decomposed.

Determine how long it will take for 90% of the substance to decompose.
items.sol:
Half decomposes after $24$ hours, so $M=15$ when $t=24$.
$$\begin{aligned} 15 &= 30e^{-24k} \\ e^{-24k} &= \dfrac{1}{2} \\ k &= \dfrac{\ln2}{24} \end{aligned}$$
$90\%$ decomposed leaves $10\%$, so $M=3$.
$$\begin{aligned} 3 &= 30e^{-kt} \\ e^{-kt} &= \dfrac{1}{10} \\ t &= \dfrac{\ln10}{k} \\ &= \dfrac{24\ln10}{\ln2} \\ &\approx79.7 \text{ hours} \end{aligned}$$

items.part: Find the value of $a$ and $b$ if $\left(2\sqrt{3}+3\right)^2+\dfrac{1}{2-\sqrt{3}}=a+b\sqrt{3}$
items.sol:

$$\begin{aligned}\text{LHS}&=\left(2\sqrt{3}+3\right)^2+\dfrac{1}{2-\sqrt{3}}\times\dfrac{2+\sqrt{3}}{2+\sqrt{3}}\\&=12+12\sqrt{3}+9+2+\sqrt{3}\\&=23+13\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore a=23,\ b=13$$

items.part:
Coal is extracted from a mine at a rate that is proportional to the amount of coal remaining in the mine. Hence the amount $R$ remaining after $t$ years is given by $R=R_0e^{-kt}$, where $k$ is a constant and $R_0$ is the initial amount of coal.

After 20 years, $50\%$ of the initial amount of coal remains.
How many more years will elapse before only $10\%$ of the original amount remains?
items.sol:
From part (i), $k=\dfrac{1}{20}\ln 2$. Set $R=0.1R_0$ and solve for $t$.
$$\begin{aligned}0.1R_0&=R_0e^{-\frac{1}{20}\ln 2\times t}\\ 0.1&=e^{-\frac{1}{20}\ln 2\times t}\\ \ln(0.1)&=\ln e^{-\frac{1}{20}\ln 2\times t}\\ -\dfrac{1}{20}\ln 2\times t&=-\ln 10\\ t&=\dfrac{20\ln 10}{\ln 2}\\ &\approx 66.44\end{aligned}$$
The question asks for how many more years, so subtract the first 20 years.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{More years}&=66.44-20\\ &=46.44\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{about } 46.44 \text{ more years}$$

items.part:
The graph of $y = \sqrt{x}$ undergoes the following sequence of transformations:

\begin{itemize}
\item Translation 3 units right
\item Dilation horizontally by a factor of $\dfrac{1}{2}$
\item Translation 1 unit down
\item Dilation vertically by a factor of 4
\end{itemize}

Find the equation of the resulting graph.
items.sol:
Apply each transformation in order.

Translation 3 units right replaces $x$ with $x-3$:

$$y = \sqrt{x-3}$$

Dilation horizontally by a factor of $\dfrac{1}{2}$ replaces $x$ with $2x$:

$$y = \sqrt{2x-3}$$

Translation 1 unit down subtracts 1:

$$y = \sqrt{2x-3} - 1$$

Dilation vertically by a factor of 4 multiplies $y$ by 4:

$$y = 4\sqrt{2x-3} - 4$$

Equivalently, $y = \sqrt{32x-48} - 4$.

items.part: Find the equation of the normal to the curve $y = \dfrac{\ln(x - 1)}{x - 1}$ at the point $(2,0)$.
items.sol:
Using the quotient rule, $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{u}{v}\right)=\dfrac{u'v-uv'}{v^2}$, with
$$\begin{aligned} u&=\ln(x-1) & v&=x-1\\ u'&=\dfrac{1}{x-1} & v'&=1 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} y'&=\dfrac{(x-1)\left(\frac{1}{x-1}\right)-\ln(x-1)(1)}{(x-1)^2}\\ &=\dfrac{1-\ln(x-1)}{(x-1)^2} \end{aligned}$$
Substitute $x=2$:
$$\begin{aligned} y'&=\dfrac{1-\ln(2-1)}{(2-1)^2}\\ &=1-\ln 1\\ &=1 \end{aligned}$$
$\therefore m_T=1$ and $m_N=-1$

Equation of the normal:
$$\begin{aligned} y-0&=-1(x-2)\\ y&=-x+2 \end{aligned}$$

Write an expression for the minimum value of the function $g(x) = 1 - f(x)$ over the domain $[a,b]$ .
items.sol:

items.part:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two events such that $P(X)=0.5$, $P(Y)=0.6$ and $P(Y\mid X)=0.7$.
Determine whether $X$ and $Y$ are independent events.
items.sol:
Using the conditional probability formula:
$$\begin{aligned}P(Y\mid X)&=\dfrac{P(Y\cap X)}{P(X)}\\ 0.7&=\dfrac{P(Y\cap X)}{0.5}\\ P(Y\cap X)&=0.35\end{aligned}$$
For independence we need $P(X)\times P(Y)=P(X\cap Y)$.
$$\begin{aligned}P(Y)\times P(X)&=0.5\times0.6\\ &=0.3\\ &\ne P(Y\cap X)\end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ $X$ and $Y$ are not independent.

items.part:
The Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) of Hawaii is $-10$ hours.

When it is 9 pm Wednesday in Hawaii, it is 12:30 pm Thursday in India.

What is the UTC of India?
items.sol:
Hawaii is UTC$-10$, so UTC time is $10$ hours ahead of Hawaii time.
$$9\text{ pm Wednesday} + 10 \text{ h} = 7\text{ am Thursday (UTC)}$$
India's time is $12:30$ pm Thursday, so India is ahead of UTC by
$$12:30 - 7:00 = 5\text{ h }30\text{ min}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the UTC of India is } +5{:}30 \text{ (UTC } +5.5)$$

items.part:
The perimeter of a rectangle is 390 cm and the side lengths are in the ratio $9:4$.

What is the area of the rectangle?
items.sol:
\exfigure{5836_q28_s1}

Let the sides be $9x$ and $4x$. The perimeter is
$$\begin{aligned} P &= 9x + 4x + 9x + 4x \\ &= 26x \end{aligned}$$
Since $P = 390$:
$$\begin{aligned} 26x &= 390 \\ x &= \dfrac{390}{26} = 15 \end{aligned}$$
Hence
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Length} &= 9 \times 15 = 135 \\ \text{Width} &= 4 \times 15 = 60 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Area} &= \text{Length} \times \text{Width} \\ &= 135 \times 60 \\ &= 8100 \text{ cm}^2 \end{aligned}$$

Energy used is power in kW times hours. Three months is $\dfrac{52}{4}=13$ weeks.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{electricity used} &= 0.4\times 8\times 6\times \dfrac{52}{4} \\ &= 249.6 \text{ kWh}\end{aligned}$$
At $25.2$ c/kWh $=\$0.252$/kWh:
$$\begin{aligned}\text{cost} &= 249.6\times 0.252 \\ &= 62.8992\ldots \\ &= \$62.90 \text{ (to the nearest cent)}\end{aligned}$$
